Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying op-
timization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on
recovering equations that describe observed input–output patterns. We introduce
OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic
optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that
infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an
optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agen-
tic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical
priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying
mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on
OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems,

The Optimization Learner represents observational data as an optimization problem, but the learned
representation is not yet a compact symbolic law. The Optimization Discoverer (OptDiscover)
addresses this by extracting the symbolic form of the learned optimization problem, as illustrated
in Figure 1 (a,b). After OptLearner is trained, its parameters are frozen. OptDiscover then distills
the components of the optimization representation bottleneck into compact symbolic expressions.
This bottleneck consists of three types of components: objective terms Uθ, inequality-constraint
terms Cθ, and equality-constraint terms Tθ, with each type optionally comprising multiple branches.
OptDiscover searches for a compact symbolic expression for each active component,

evidence.excerpt:
We evaluate OptScientist Model onOptFeynman, a new benchmark for optimization-law discov-
ery, and the full framework on two real-world scientific-discovery tasks, with comparisons against
machine-learning models, symbolic regression, and LLM model-discovery methods. The LLM base-
lines include an LLM-only researcher, GeCCo (Rmus et al., 2026) as a code-assisted LLM approach,
and Model Discovery Agent (MDA; Murphy, 2026) as a Bayesian experiment-design approach. All
LLM methods use DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the same LLM used by the optional OptScientist Agent. Data
and evaluation are provided in Sec. 5, and comparison methods in Appendix B.1.

Limitations and Future Research.When the structure of ground-truth models deviates substantially
from an optimization formulation, our approach is likely to fail. Although, mathematically, a broad
class of laws not originally formulated as optimization problems can be represented in optimization
form, the OptFeynman results show that OptScientist can recover the original laws from such
representations. Future research is needed to characterize the limits of the optimization assumption
and identify the classes of models that remain discoverable within a feasible computational budget.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: OptFeynman provides analytic ground-truth objectives, and evaluation uses held-out contexts with neutral variable identifiers and deterministic post-selection metrics, so the reported gains are measured against objective external references rather than the training or distillation signals [E36faff0f38e38439-B0054, E36faff0f38e38439-B0058, E36faff0f38e38439-B0148].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established on held-out test contexts using exact-order and pairwise preference accuracy against known ground-truth objectives, KL divergence to ground-truth Gibbs distributions, and out-of-time predictive accuracy on real-world tasks [E36faff0f38e38439-B0036, E36faff0f38e38439-B0059, E36faff0f38e38439-B0148, E36faff0f38e38439-B0168].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: OptLearner is trained with cross-entropy or sampled contrastive Gibbs loss on training data, and OptDiscover fits symbolic expressions by minimizing distillation MSE against frozen bottleneck component outputs [E36faff0f38e38439-B0024, E36faff0f38e38439-B0026, E36faff0f38e38439-B0085].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims of superior exact-order recovery on OptFeynman (e.g., 88.9% discrete and 78.8% continuous) and competitive predictive accuracy with high parameter and token efficiency on empirical tasks are well-supported by reported quantitative tables and ablation details [E36faff0f38e38439-B0003, E36faff0f38e38439-B0047, E36faff0f38e38439-B0051, E36faff0f38e38439-B0128, E36faff0f38e38439-B0168].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is comprehensive across OptFeynman (a synthetic physics benchmark of 99 problems across discrete and continuous settings under clean and noisy contexts) and two real-world empirical tasks (risky choice and central-bank policy), comparing against diverse baselines on held-out context sets using exact-order accuracy, KL divergence, and predictive metrics [E36faff0f38e38439-B0034, E36faff0f38e38439-B0036, E36faff0f38e38439-B0040, E36faff0f38e38439-B0054, E36faff0f38e38439-B0059, E36faff0f38e38439-B0128, E36faff0f38e38439-B0140].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using objective ground-truth preference orderings from analytic equations on held-out test splits with neutral variable identifiers and deterministic post-selection metrics [E36faff0f38e38439-B0054, E36faff0f38e38439-B0059, E36faff0f38e38439-B0148].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out context exact-order recovery, pairwise accuracy, KL divergence against ground-truth physics formulas, and out-of-time test predictive accuracy on real-world datasets [E36faff0f38e38439-B0036, E36faff0f38e38439-B0059, E36faff0f38e38439-B0148, E36faff0f38e38439-B0168].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training and validation losses from contrastive/cross-entropy Gibbs loss on training data, coupled with distillation MSE to fit symbolic expressions to bottleneck layers [E36faff0f38e38439-B0024, E36faff0f38e38439-B0026, E36faff0f38e38439-B0085].

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations, noting that the method relies on phenomena admitting an underlying optimization formulation and noting bounds when phenomena diverge fundamentally from optimization mechanics [E36faff0f38e38439-B0066].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the Behavior Learning backbone, contrastive and cross-entropy Gibbs objectives, symbolic distillation via regression over frozen latent bottleneck layers, and multi-agent coordination protocols [E36faff0f38e38439-B0021, E36faff0f38e38439-B0026, E36faff0f38e38439-B0031].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides a well-formulated scientific contribution, rigorous mathematical foundations, clear architectural specifics, and strong empirical validation across a broad benchmark and real-world datasets with adequate controls and baselines [E36faff0f38e38439-B0007, E36faff0f38e38439-B0034, E36faff0f38e38439-B0128].
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces OptScientist, an automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from observational data, combining a two-stage neural representation and distillation model (OptLearner and OptDiscover) with an iterative LLM-agentic workflow [E36faff0f38e38439-B0002, E36faff0f38e38439-B0007, E36faff0f38e38439-B0008].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides a well-formulated scientific contribution, rigorous mathematical foundations, clear architectural specifics, and strong empirical validation across a broad benchmark and real-world datasets with adequate controls and baselines [E36faff0f38e38439-B0007, E36faff0f38e38439-B0034, E36faff0f38e38439-B0128].
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations, noting that the method relies on phenomena admitting an underlying optimization formulation and noting bounds when phenomena diverge fundamentally from optimization mechanics [E36faff0f38e38439-B0066].
